title: Developing the Superpower of Curiosity
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The piece argues that curiosity is the closest thing a leader has to a superpower and that it can be deliberately grown rather than merely possessed. It links curiosity to the personality trait of Openness to Experience, then reverses the usual causal arrow: novel experiences also build curiosity. Its central move is to rank experiences, claiming that open-ended learning experiences that pair an enjoyable activity with a complex subject do more for curiosity than novelty alone. It offers concrete examples such as modeling the night sky to learn astronomy or making ice cream to learn physics. The piece closes with a Walt Disney line to show that curiosity and interesting activity feed each other.
points: Curiosity and Openness to Experience reinforce each other, so leaders can raise curiosity by deliberately seeking novelty rather than waiting for a trait to appear.
Open-ended learning experiences outperform simple novelty because the activity itself is a vehicle for learning a complex subject.
The examples (astronomy models, ice cream physics, battlefield reenactment) show how a leader can design curiosity-building experiences of their own.
quotes: If a leadership superpower does exist, it must be curiosity. Many of the most successful leaders and entrepreneurs point to their seemingly innate curiosity as the basis for their success. If curiosity is indeed the wonder drug of insight, learning, and relationships, the question becomes how to enhance it.
Of the big five factors of personality, the trait of Openness to Experience is most connected to curiosity. This factor emphasizes imagination and eagerness to learn new things.

When people engage in novel experiences, they enhance their natural curiosity to seek out more. Listening to new kinds of music, traveling to places one has never been to, discovering new restaurants or local attractions, experimenting with new foods and tastes, and walking through interesting landscapes and parks are all examples of experiences that strengthen curiosity.

But not all experiences are created equal when it comes to boosting curiosity. In addition to novel experiences, open-ended learning experiences are even more powerful for developing an inquisitive mind.
These experiences marry an enjoyable activity with learning about a complex subject. Curiosity is baked into the experience when people use them to learn about something else.

Seeking novel and open-ended learning experiences is one way to light the fire of curiosity. In the words of the imaginative Walt Disney, “When you’re curious, you find lots of interesting things to do.” The funny thing is, finding interesting things to do makes you more curious, as well.
